JWT + Key Material Generator 🔐

Generate strong HMAC secrets, Ed25519 PEM keypairs, RSA/EC signing keys, and copy-ready env blocks entirely in your browser. Private material stays on-device and is persisted locally so you can come back later without doing the raccoon-memory routine.

Generator

Use HMAC mode for HS256/HS512. Use keypair mode for Ed25519, RS256, or ES256-style workflows.

Switching modes changes the controls and output shape.
Saved with the generated item so future-you knows what this thing actually was.
For most .env files, base64url is the cleanest.
More bytes = more entropy. Do not cheap out and summon weak randomness goblins.
64 bytes • 512 bits
Common picks: 32 (ok), 64 (strong), 96–128 (overkill in a good way).
Ed25519 is compact and modern. RSA/EC help with older ecosystems.
Builds private/public env variable names automatically.
Browser generates the PEMs directly; snippets are copy-ready alternates.
PEM mode: this app exports real PKCS#8 private keys and SPKI public keys in valid PEM wrappers. That means the output is usable as env content for things like SBOM_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM and SBOM_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY_PEM.
Strength: —
Storage note: this app now persists its vault in localStorage on this browser/device. That is convenient, but if you are on a shared machine, clear the vault when you are done being powerful.

Current Output

The main output changes with mode. For secrets you get one value. For keypairs you get PEMs, env blocks, and tooling snippets.

Browser-generated PEMs are real. The helper snippets still exist, and the new browser runner can execute a supported OpenSSL-style lane for key generation/export without shipping the native OpenSSL binary.

OpenSSL-style Browser Runner + Export Studio

Run supported OpenSSL-style key-generation commands directly in-browser, then export the current item or the full vault as JSON, TXT, HTML, PDF, or DOCX.

This single-file app does not embed the native OpenSSL binary. It runs a supported OpenSSL-compatible browser lane backed by Web Crypto for key generation and PEM export.
Load a vault item into the current view first if you want to export one specific saved item.
PDF and DOCX exports are built in-browser so you can archive or hand off the generated material cleanly.

Mini Suite Bridge — Sovereign Variables

Push the current secret/keypair or the whole vault into Sovereign Variables for secure variable packaging and storage. Sovereign can also push active environment packs back into this app as browser workspace files.

Outbound lane: generated secrets and PEM env blocks can be queued straight into Sovereign Variables so users can secure, organize, and package them as environment vessels.
Inbound lane: Sovereign pushes active environment packs back into this app as queued .env workspace files for the browser runner and export studio.
Sovereign intake: 0 queued packages in Sovereign Variables.
JWT suite intake: 0 queued environment packs from Sovereign.

Vault (persistent local history)

Your original file had an in-memory history view, but not real persistence. This upgrade stores the vault locally so the items are still there after refreshes and restarts. fileciteturn1file1

The vault is local-only unless you export it yourself.

Usage notes

The original app was strictly an HMAC secret generator with prefixing and a simple history display. This upgrade keeps that flow and adds proper PEM keypair generation and copy-ready env material. fileciteturn1file0turn1file2

For JWT HMAC: use secret mode and put the output in something like JWT_SECRET.
For SBOM signing: use PEM keypair mode with the SBOM signing env preset and copy the env block.
For shared machines: local persistence is convenient, but convenience and paranoia are cousins for a reason. Clear the vault when needed.
For OpenSSL/other tooling: this app now gives you copy-ready snippets, a browser OpenSSL-style runner, and export lanes for HTML, PDF, and DOCX handoff.
Built as a single-file app. Drop it on Netlify as index.html and you’re live. ⚡
